text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.5% today to close at $371.97, continuing a sharp downward trend over the past week that has wiped out 10% of its value since mid-November. The decline coincides with a significant drop in oil prices—US crude is trading at $89.53 per barrel, down from levels above $100 just days ago—which directly pressures refining company margins. While US refineries are running at a high 95.7% capacity, the collapse in crude prices means less profit per barrel of fuel produced.

The broader context suggests a pullback from geopolitical risk premiums that had likely supported oil earlier. Reports about Iran's military actions against US positions in the Gulf and threats to Strait of Hormuz shipping drove concerns in mid-November, but those fears appear to have faded as markets reassessed the actual disruption risk. With oil prices normalizing lower and no new supply disruptions materializing, the refining sector has lost the tailwind that had buoyed it.
